stem: Which figure is the **starting point** of a partnership appropriation account?

options.rationale: Correct: the appropriation account shares the profit after all expenses.
Expenses must be deducted first, in the income statement.
Revenue is the first line of the income statement, not of the appropriation account.
Capital is used to calculate interest; it is not the starting point.

explanation: The appropriation account begins with the profit (or loss) for the year from the income statement.

stem: How is **interest on drawings** shown in a partnership appropriation account?

options.content: Added to the profit for the year
options.rationale: Correct: partners pay it, so more profit is available to share.

options.content: Deducted from the profit for the year
options.rationale: Interest on capital is deducted; interest on drawings is added.

options.content: Shown as an expense in the income statement
options.rationale: It is an appropriation item, not an expense.

options.content: Credited to the partners' capital accounts
options.rationale: It is charged to (debited to) the partners.

explanation: Interest on drawings is a charge on the partners: add it in the appropriation account and debit each partner's current account.

stem: Which item is **not** shown in a partnership appropriation account?

options.rationale: Correct: it is an expense in the income statement.
This is an appropriation of profit.
Partners' salaries are appropriations.

options.content: Each partner's share of the residual profit
options.rationale: This is the final section of the appropriation account.

explanation: A partner's loan is a liability; its interest is deducted before the profit for the year.

stem: Profit for the year US\$26,850; interest on capital US\$3,150; partners' salaries US\$5,400; interest on drawings US\$420. What is the residual profit?

options.rationale: Interest on drawings has been deducted instead of added.
Interest on drawings has been left out.
The salaries have not been deducted.

hints: Which item is added and which items are deducted?

stem: The residual profit of US\$19,250 is shared between Farai and Rudo in the ratio 4 : 3. What is Rudo's share?

options.rationale: This is Farai's share (4/7).
The ratio has been read as 3/4 instead of 3/7.
This is an equal share, ignoring the ratio.

stem: Interest on drawings is charged at 10% a year. Tendai drew US\$7,200 on 1 October 2025. The year ends on 31 December 2025. What is the interest on these drawings?

options.rationale: This charges a full year's interest.
This counts the nine months before the drawing, not the three after it.
This charges one month only.

hints: Count the months from the date of drawing to the year end.

stem: Thandeka's capital was US\$30,000 on 1 January 2025. She introduced a further US\$12,000 on 1 July 2025. Interest on capital is 8% a year. What is her interest on capital for 2025?

options.rationale: The new capital has been given a full year's interest.
Correct: 2,400 on the opening capital plus 480 on the new capital for six months.
The new capital has been ignored.
All the capital has been given six months' interest.

hints: Treat the two amounts of capital separately and time each one.

stem: Partners A and B share profits equally. The agreement is changed so that B receives a salary. If the profit for the year is unchanged, what happens to A's share of the **residual** profit?

options.rationale: The salary is deducted before the residual profit is shared.

options.content: It falls by the full salary
options.rationale: B also bears half of the reduction in residual profit.

options.content: It falls by half of the salary
options.rationale: Correct: the salary reduces the residual profit, which A shares equally with B.

options.content: It rises by half of the salary
options.rationale: Deducting an appropriation cannot raise the residual profit.

explanation: The salary comes out of the profit before sharing, so the residual falls by the salary and A bears half of that fall.
hints: The salary is deducted before the residual profit is shared.

stem: If interest on capital and salaries are greater than the profit for the year, the partners share a residual loss.
explanation: True. Interest and salaries are given in full; the shortfall is a residual loss shared in the profit-sharing ratio.

stem: Interest on drawings is credited to the partners' current accounts.
explanation: False. It is a charge on the partners, so it is debited to their current accounts and added in the appropriation account.

stem: Match each partnership item with where it is recorded.

right.content: Debited to the current account only

explanation: Interest on drawings is added; interest on capital and salaries are deducted; loan interest is an expense; drawings themselves go straight to the current account.
hints: Only one item never passes through the appropriation account or the income statement.

stem: Complete the order of the appropriation account.

payload.template: Profit for the year, {{blank:a}} interest on drawings, {{blank:b}} interest on capital and salaries, giving the {{blank:c}} profit, which is shared in the {{blank:d}}.

explanation: Add interest on drawings, deduct interest on capital and salaries, and share the residual profit in the profit-sharing ratio.

stem: Interest on drawings is charged at 12% a year; the year ends on 31 December 2025. Sipho drew US\$3,600 on 1 April 2025 and US\$2,700 on 1 September 2025. Calculate his total interest on drawings.
explanation: 3,600 × 12% × 9/12 = 324; 2,700 × 12% × 4/12 = 108. Total 432. Charging a full year on all drawings gives 756.
workedSolution: 1. 3,600 × 12% × 9/12 = 324; 2,700 × 12% × 4/12 = 108. Total 432. Charging a full year on all drawings gives 756.
hints: 1 April to 31 December is 9 months; 1 September to 31 December is 4 months.

stem: Profit for the year US\$22,680. Interest on drawings: Rudo US\$180, Chipo US\$300. Interest on capital: Rudo US\$2,250, Chipo US\$1,350. Salary: Chipo US\$6,000. Residual profit shared Rudo 3 : Chipo 1. Calculate the **total** amount credited to Chipo from the appropriation account (interest on capital, salary and share of profit).
explanation: Residual = 22,680 + 480 − 3,600 − 6,000 = 13,560; Chipo's share = 3,390. Credited: 1,350 + 6,000 + 3,390 = 10,740. Her interest on drawings (300) is a separate debit in her current account.
workedSolution: 1. Residual = 22,680 + 480 − 3,600 − 6,000 = 13,560; Chipo's share = 3,390. Credited: 1,350 + 6,000 + 3,390 = 10,740. Her interest on drawings (300) is a separate debit in her current account.
hints: Find the residual profit first, then Chipo's quarter of it.

stem: A partnership's appropriation account shows: interest on capital US\$1,600 and US\$1,200; salary US\$3,000; interest on drawings US\$250 and US\$150; shares of residual profit US\$5,880 and US\$3,920. Calculate the profit for the year.
explanation: Profit = interest on capital 2,800 + salary 3,000 + shares 9,800 − interest on drawings 400 = 15,200. Adding the interest on drawings instead gives 16,000.
workedSolution: 1. Profit = interest on capital 2,800 + salary 3,000 + shares 9,800 − interest on drawings 400 = 15,200. Adding the interest on drawings instead gives 16,000.
hints: Work backwards: what was added to the profit, and what was taken from it?

stem: Explain why interest on capital is **not** treated as an expense of a partnership.

points.description: It is not a cost of running the business / no money is paid to an outsider
It is a way of sharing the profit between the owners (an appropriation)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Interest on capital is a reward to the owners for their investment; it divides the profit between them rather than being a cost of earning that profit, so it is an appropriation.

explanation: Appropriations share profit between owners; expenses are costs of earning it.

stem: Nyasha says: "We made a profit of US\$9,000, but after paying ourselves salaries of US\$12,000 we have a loss. We should stop paying salaries." Comment on her statement.

points.description: The business still made a profit of US\$9,000; the salaries are appropriations, not expenses
The residual loss of US\$3,000 is simply shared in the profit-sharing ratio
Conclusion: salaries only change how the profit is divided; they could be reduced if they are unfair, but they do not cause a business loss

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The business made a profit of US\$9,000. Partners' salaries share that profit out; they are not costs. The US\$3,000 shortfall is a residual loss shared in the ratio, which only shifts profit between partners. Salaries could be reviewed for fairness, but stopping them would not make the business more profitable.

explanation: Appropriations change the division of profit, not its size.
hints: Is a partner's salary an expense or an appropriation?
